Suppose $A_n$ and $B_n$ are two independent $n times n$ Hermitian random matrices.

Assume that, as $n \to \infty$, we understand the eigenvalues of each matrix separately. Perhaps their empirical spectral distributions converge to measures $\mu_A$ and $\mu_B$.

What should we expect from $A_n + B_n$?

At first this sounds like it ought to be easy. The difficulty is that matrices have eigenvectors.
